title: Reflex Arena
description: Changelog and events of Reflex Arena

items.title: 1.3.1 – Free to Play
items.content_html:
Hey team!

As promised, we're moving to a free-to-play model, giving back to the community after all these years! We're also working on setting up a curated workshop for weapon skins (and potentially models), but wanted to get this point release out for the F2P launch.


Gameplay

  • Implemented zoom weapon FOV

  • Implemented spawn point visibility during warmup

  • Fixed positional audio not working correctly on some machines

  • Players are no longer auto re-queued in matchmaking when missing a pop


Forge

  • Fixed custom skin issues introduced in the 1.3.0 rebuild


Backend

  • No longer upgrade official servers while players are on them

  • Fixed invalid queue timeout (was causing longer-than-expected queues)

Cheers,
Shooter

items.title: 1.3.0 - Reflex Reloaded
items.content_html:
Hey all!

This update brings matchmaking back to life along with a bunch of quality of life (QoL) improvements.

Also will be going free to play (soon), so spread the word if you know anyone who might enjoy it.

It's been fun getting back into Reflex. Thanks to the community for sticking around throughout the years! <3

Community:
- Added #bug-reports to discord, where players can report / upvote bugs
- Added #feedback-and-suggestions to discord, where players can report / upvote features
- Join discord here -> https://discord.gg/reflex

QoL menu:
- updated menu music
- added training to home screen to guide new players
- training maps now progress automatically through the end of map scoreboard
- server browser can now mark servers as favorites
- server browser remembers your last sorting column

QoL game:
- updated ruleset to CR2
- added player weapon zoom
- chat log is now scrollable
- mutators no longer resurrect dead players if they deal damage after dying
- floating damage text now support scaling
- smoother `r_showfps` display
- reduced default volume levels
- better default weapon bindings
- bots now change off guns with no ammo
- spectator muting option: sv_mutespecs / callvote mutespecs

QoL rendering:
- r_monitor to select output monitor
- fixed bunch of alt-tabbing issues
- allow very high resolutions on Windows (5K2K monitors)
- added borderless windowed
- default resolution now 1080p

Matchmaking/Server:
- new matchmaking system - see reflextracker.gg
- official servers back online eu central + us west + us east
- redesigned matchmaking screen with MMR display
- Dedicated server now available for Linux
- MM is one click play with skill-matched bots (bots optional)

Stability & Performance:
- numerous crash fixes
- smoother performance profiler display
- uploaded steamworks lib, newer workshop maps load correctly now
- fixed fonts not being loaded properly resulting in fallbacks in Wine

Addons:
- .effect asset file had to be changed with 64bit upgrade, if you're overriding assets in addons they will fail to load now
- PlayerSpeed widget: option to hide "ups" unit text
- PlayerSpeed/MovementKeys widgets: race-only toggle

Under the hood eng changes:
- brought engine/repo back to life
- 32bit -> 64bit exe upgrade
- updated PhysX 3.3 -> 5.0, LuaJIT, Steamworks etc (required as libs were too dated)
- new crash reporter
- new MM backend

Note:
- If you need to access the old build, in steam right click reflex -> properties -> beta -> betacode: legacyreflex

-- Shooter

title: Reflex Racing
description: Reflex Arena race mode community news

items.title: About leaderboards moderation
items.content_html:
We're finally near to bring closure to a heated debate that's been around ever since the leaderboards came out over 10 years ago.

Before we begin I want to emphasize that this is an important topic for many people including myself and will be treated as such on public channels. Lots of compromises were made for setting the example of what this community can achieve and I'm grateful to anyone who stands for this cause.

Timeline

The racing community started to form right after the release of alpha version 0.34.0 that introduced the race mode, with mappers releasing many projects and racers dedicating themselves to achieve the fastest times.

We kept track of scores by screenshots and word of mouth on public servers because there were no leaderboards available back then.

Everyone wanted to be included in the grind but with servers being absolutely packed it was clear people couldn't keep up with all the records, so after a few attempts at a community-made leaderboards system, the breakthrough came from brandon in 2016 and his Race Leaderboards addon that actually brought the steamworks API to light and became an essential part of Reflex race even to this day.

It also brought evidence of the extent of people taking credit of records achieved with casual play to those who wanted a fair competition, so much that it made moderating the leaderboards a top priority. But this was easier said than done because:

  1. We didn't have a community network.
  2. Developers had just left the game so updates could only be made on already archived versions of the leaderboards and not on the official database.

In order to solve that, we first had to address the community network which back then was limited to a channel on the official Reflex Arena discord and a race section on the forums that was eventually taken down and lost.

So when I created the Reflex Racing discord in 2018, lolograde and I started working on the first Reflex Racing World Cup. This is important to the topic because it brought the first list of community rules and guidelines to the players.

Competitive Racing Ruleset

These are the fundamental rules of our tournaments that players have to follow:

1. Maps must not be edited.
2. Only the correct physics ruleset must be used as explicitly required by the map.
3. No wallbugs or any other game-breaking glitches can be used.
4. Time-resets that involve going back to the start line after crossing its border are not allowed.

Many people, starting from the WM clan which purpose is to promote fair competitive play, abide by these rules on public matches too.

The main issue with public leaderboards is that both casual and comp players are ranked together and there is no way to differentiate these records unless actually looking at the replays, which can only be accessed when shared by the players themselves.

In the last 10 years we did our best to promote these rules of conduct to the community, but had no way to enforce them outside of our tournaments.

So now that (1) we have an established racing community network and (2) the main dev returned to Reflex from his leave, we can actually solve this problem once and for all.

Solution #1: Community sovereignty

Since the reflex.racing leaderboards are now separated from the official database, this solution treats the race community as independent from the game and involves filtering the datasets to include comp players only.

A grace period of 1 month would be announced to give casual players the chance of overwriting their records without registering on the activity feed.

After that, any player caught holding at least 1 record not following comp guidelines will be blacklisted from the website and rankings will be recalculated without their records.

Players are advised to save a replay for each record to prove the legitimacy of their runs with the reflex.racing admins at any time.

Banned players are not allowed to appeal their ban as long as the current game version doesn't include a remediation for that specific exploit, following either with a verified manual overwrite of their records or a leaderboards reset.

In the event of the community scaling up, a whitelist system may be implemented instead.

For your information, there is a list of offenders ready to be banned, gathered from the recent census of maps, public replays and matches over the years.

This system however should be considered only if the following solution #2 is not applicable in a relative short amount of time.

Solution #2: Ruleset creation

Some solutions for the 4 exploits mentioned above can include:

  1. Checking if the map hash is equal to the latest version of map currently available on the Steam workshop and preventing records from saving during editor enabled matches.
  2. Add physics changing brushes that players can walk into and remove the option to vote for them.
  3. Add slick surfaces and force a conversion on walls within a certain inclination to retroactively update all maps. First tried with kawumm's slick mod.
  4. Disable time-resets after crossing the start brush.

This is in the hands of shooter and I'm not aware of his backlog so I can't tell how long it will take to implement, just my opinion on what can be done to fix these issues.

But how will applying all these fixes affect the current leaderboards?

This is critical because it would require either a complete reset of the leaderboards to free all maps from old unmoderated records,

Note that no records will be lost! The current network is already keeping track of our entire record history outside of the game and even once the reset is applied, those leaderboards will still be archived on the datasets.

OR, creating an actual Competitive Racing Ruleset that people can switch to whenever they want.

This ruleset would include the fixes listed above and would only save records on a new, separate leaderboard for each map, leaving casual and unmoderated records as they are.

Some degree of measures will have to be considered to prevent people from saving casual records on comp leaderboards, and having the ability to remove those that did.

///

This is a great long-term solution to ensure keeping the community together and engaged, since all records achieved using this new competitive ruleset will be saved on the current official steamworks database, just with a different name for each leaderboards table.

For instance, given the current leaderboards tables are called mapid.race, the comp ruleset would just save to a new empty mapid_crr.race table to the database.

No need to force manual overwrites, resets or making anyone learn a list of rules in order to avoid a ban.

Conclusion

It all comes down to choosing one of these 2 options:

  1. Apply solution #1 and move forward with independent control, forming a new racing community.
  2. Wait for shooter to release a race comp ruleset, then serve both casual and comp leaderboards on the reflex.racing website.

Second option is preferable but with the free-to-play release, casual play may increase to uncontrollable levels if this issue is not addressed right away.

So I'm asking for shooter to kindly confirm whether that ruleset solution can be applied in a relative short amount of time, let's say by the end of the year, otherwise I will have to proceed with the first option.

Thank you all for supporting this community!

-htp

items.title: New website, more content!
items.content_html:
Hey everyone!

It's been a bit of a grind, but we finally got our new reflex.racing network up and running just in time to celebrate 10 years of WM.

You are probably wondering what's changed since the previous website version was halted in February so let's just get to it.

Enhanced leaderboards

No more manual updates, we now have a docker container spinning every 20 minutes to automatically pull, filter and extend the leaderboards with extra features such as:

  1. New ranking system
  2. Activity monitoring
  3. Name censoring and input sanitization
  4. Players/Maps public data from Steam (updated once a day at around 12pm UTC)

These datasets are all archived on github and can be easily verified to ensure they were not tampered with.

The website also translates ^# color codes in names for better reading.

Steam players data only concerns the username, avatar and country when available and publicly accessible at the time of the refresh.

Map properties

About 99% of all maps now include a difficulty grade and a list of badges that show what tech you can expect to find in them.

This is useful if you're looking for a specific type of map to play or even discover old forgotten gems, since the game browser doesn't show which maps are strafe only, have particular design features or how difficult they can be.

Difficulty grades are based on a number from 1 to 7 as score prefix:

1 : Training maps

This grade represents all maps that can't be categorized as time trials since they can include multiple finish lines and are usually ports or just made to be broken.

2 : Beginner maps

These maps are the easiest type of time trials and can be completed just by walking.

3 : Easy maps

Can include few easy obstacles that require clearing for completing the map.

4 : Intermediate maps

They require some technical knowledge to be completed.

5 : Advanced maps

These are mostly technical time trials that require a high level of skills to be completed.

6 : Expert maps

This is the most difficult level of time trials as it requires extensive technical and route knowledge.

7 : Challenge maps

These are maps made out of a very challenging obstacle course that require precise execution on every single section.

///

Then there's the suffix that shows how much effort is expected by using a character a-b-c:

a : Low effort

This category includes a low amount of obstacles and/or a short distance to the finish line.

b : Medium effort

Requires some degree of attention to keep the pace going.

c : High effort

Maps of extended length require a high level of attention to keep the pace.

Ranking system

The previous system only took the number of world records into consideration for global rankings since we didn't have difficulty grades available.

Now we can just calculate a score for each record, collect them for each player and sort the list:

(for each map)

playerScore += (playersCount / playerRank) * difficultyScore

This system rewards players that actually spend time grinding instead of just accumulating WRs on empty maps, and does not scale with a reltime to allow very quick records and map breaking skips.

However, considering this system can introduce bias, we are open to change difficulty grades given feedback from enough players.

News portals

This blog will be used by the reflex.racing admins to update the community on features development progress, guideline changes, upcoming events and casual racing topics.

There is also a wiki available, dedicated entirely to Reflex Arena race mode that's still being worked on.

Road to records moderation

Now for the tricky part.

As of this post date, hosted leaderboards are still unmoderated just as they appear in-game, but this is going to change soon.

My next post will address a way to differentiate casual and competitive racing as a very much needed feature for the next game update, with a fallback plan that could completely reshuffle the rankings by removing cheaters from the datasets. For now there is no need to do anything, take your time to explore the website and play more Reflex!

-htp
